stem: A solutions architect must determine which storage layer needs an automated capacity-expansion process, such as a CloudWatch alarm triggering a resize, versus which layers already scale on their own.

choices.text: An S3 bucket holding uploaded objects
An EFS file system mounted by multiple instances
An EBS volume backing a database instance

rationale: An EBS volume stays at its provisioned size and performance until it is resized, so it is the layer that needs an automated capacity-expansion process built and triggered deliberately. S3 buckets scale storage capacity automatically with nothing to provision, so there is no capacity decision to automate. EFS file systems also grow and shrink with usage automatically, with no size to provision in advance. Applying Intelligent-Tiering to an S3 bucket changes which storage class holds an object; it does not change that S3 capacity itself already scales without any automation.
